tasks.short: Contact customers, demonstrate products, explain features and seek orders.

steps.what: Review account history, open opportunities and recent orders in the {CRM}.
Select product sheets and demonstration materials from the {DOCS}.
Arrange a call or visit through {EMAIL} and the {CALENDAR}.
Demonstrate products, discuss needs, answer questions and seek an order during the visit.
Record requirements, objections and follow-up actions in the {CRM}.

loop.input: Representative's written meeting notes and the existing opportunity record.
loop.output: Proposed requirement fields, objections and follow-up actions, each linked to a note passage.
loop.check: Validate field types and account identity; the representative checks meaning and commitments before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry; unresolved fields remain blank for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes express requirements and commitments in varying language; field mapping alone loses meaning.

steps.what: Forward the order request and supporting details to the order clerk through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure an account brief in the {CRM}, assemble approved materials from the {DOCS}, and prepare appointment invitations through the {CALENDAR}. A bounded extraction loop turns written meeting notes into reviewed {CRM} updates; a configured workflow routes completed order requests to the order clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account context, product documents and order handoffs sit in separate places. Useful meeting details arrive as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing views and scheduling features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes document assembly and small integrations cheaper; bounded extraction reduces repeated typing.
tasks.still_hard: Live demonstrations, reading buying signals and resolving unfamiliar product questions require experience. Product documents must stay current.
tasks.human_edge: The representative earns trust, notices hesitation and adapts the demonstration to the buyer's situation.

ambition.what: Application-specific demonstration packs for smaller repeat customers.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less preparation and transcription, leaving room for more tailored demonstrations. Commercial approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Validate whether an order request is ready for entry.
reach.learn: Required item identifiers, quantities, delivery details and escalation rules.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad links product configuration to CRM and ERP, supporting rule-based preparation of product selections and quotes.
Written-note extraction can be bounded by field validation, source passages and human approval; live selling remains human.
In the Netherlands, seller activity monitoring can require works council consent; requirements elsewhere depend on national rules.

assumptions: The setting is a mid-size European wholesaler or manufacturer with account records in the {CRM} and approved product materials in the {DOCS}.
Visits are the representative case; remote demonstrations use similar preparation and follow-up.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings. The conversation remains the largest part.
Order routing creates an internal handoff; order acceptance follows the existing order process.
The access range includes GDPR review and applicable employee consultation under national rules. EU AI Act requirements apply where relevant.
unknowns: Whether account records contain current order history.
Whether product sheets have reliable item identifiers and approval status.
Whether contact permissions and scheduling rules are recorded.
Whether the proposed record processing requires employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing {CRM} views and appointment features cover the account brief and scheduling?
How accurately can written notes populate required fields without inventing commitments?
new_work: Review proposed meeting records and appointment invitations.
Maintain product-to-document mappings and approved templates.
Resolve incomplete order handoffs and monitor integration failures.
Sample extracted fields for omissions and incorrect commitments.

tasks.short: Find prospective customers through directories, referrals, professional networks and trade events.

steps.what: Review target segments and existing account coverage in the {CRM}.
Search business directories in {OTHER} for companies matching the target segment.
Read customer referrals in {EMAIL} and identify suggested companies and contacts.

loop.input: Selected referral messages with sender and message date.
loop.output: Suggested company, contact, referral context and supporting message passages.
loop.check: Check contact formats and company matches; a representative confirms ambiguous identities and referral meaning.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per message; ambiguous referrals enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Referrals use varied language and often imply the relationship without structured fields.

steps.what: Meet contacts at trade events and professional gatherings to discover buying needs.
Assess commercial fit and select prospects for follow-up in the {CRM}.
Check duplicates and create lead records and follow-up tasks in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure segment and territory views in the {CRM}, then import permitted structured directory data from {OTHER} with deterministic matching and provenance. A bounded loop extracts referrals from selected {EMAIL} messages; the representative qualifies prospects, while configured duplicate checks and task creation complete the records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prospect information arrives through unrelated directories, referrals and events. Manual identity matching and record entry make small prospects expensive to research.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured imports and existing duplicate checks handle routine records. AI-assisted coding lowers integration effort, while a small extraction loop handles referral language.
tasks.still_hard: Buying intent and referral strength are often known only through conversation. Directory access, permitted reuse and company identity quality vary.
tasks.human_edge: The representative recognises promising relationships and earns introductions that a directory cannot supply.

ambition.what: Small regional resellers previously below the prospect-research threshold.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time collecting and entering company details and more time developing introductions. Prospect selection remains within existing territory and qualification rights.

reach.task: Assess coverage gaps across territories and customer segments.
reach.learn: Segment definitions, territory conflicts and the difference between list size and commercial potential.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales documents lead research and qualification agents. This establishes capability, not a need for autonomous agents here.
Structured directory imports, duplicate checks and bounded referral extraction can support prospect discovery without automating networking.
GDPR applies to identifiable business contacts; outreach permissions also depend on channel and national rules.

assumptions: A permitted structured directory export or interface is available; its subscription cost is separate from build time.
The {CRM} supports lead staging, duplicate checks and follow-up tasks.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates. Networking remains the dominant activity, consistent with the relationship-heavy priors.
Qualification time falls because source evidence and existing-account matches arrive together.
The access range includes data-use review, GDPR requirements and applicable employee consultation under national rules; EU AI Act requirements apply where relevant.
unknowns: Which directory data may legally and contractually be reused.
How territory ownership and duplicate account disputes are resolved.
Whether referral messages contain usable contact details.
Which national outreach and employee consultation rules apply.
research_questions: What proportion of directory candidates match existing accounts or inactive leads?
Which qualification criteria are objective enough to display as filters?
Can ambiguous company matches be isolated without delaying clean imports?
new_work: Review ambiguous company matches and extracted referrals.
Maintain target filters, source permissions and retention rules.
Correct stale contacts and process objections or deletion requests.
Monitor import failures and directory schema changes.

tasks.short: Negotiate shelf placement, displays and advertising support with retail merchants.

steps.what: Review retailer sales, margin and previous promotional spending in the {ERP}.
Inspect shelf position, competing displays and promotional execution during a store visit.
Calculate placement options, promotional support and margin limits in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Negotiate shelf position, display duration and advertising support with the retail buyer.
Approve concessions outside the representative's mandate through {EMAIL}.
Prepare and send the written placement agreement through {DOCS} and {EMAIL}.
Record the placement agreement and execution follow-up in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Use an {ERP} performance view and a deterministic calculator to prepare placement options within recorded budgets and mandates. A form in the {WORKFLOW} captures negotiated terms, routes exceptional concessions to the sales manager, generates an agreement in the {DOCS}, and records approved commitments in the {CRM} after representative approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Retailer performance, promotional spending and commercial mandates are scattered. Informal concessions are difficult to turn into reliable records.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple calculators, structured terms and document templates cover the paperwork. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting those components.
tasks.still_hard: Retailer bargaining power, competing brands and uncertain promotional effects resist fixed rules. Sales data may not reveal actual shelf execution.
tasks.human_edge: The representative understands the buyer's pressures, trades concessions carefully and protects the long-term relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly placement-renewal choices for priority retailers.

tasks.altitude: The representative can revisit placement economics more often and spend less time assembling agreements. Existing concession limits and manager approval rights remain in place.

reach.task: Allocate promotional support across retail accounts.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, promotional attribution and how to compare placement options with uncertain outcomes.

evidence.claim: Margin calculators, mandate checks and agreement templates can automate preparation and recording without automating negotiation.
The digest provides no documented case of automated shelf-placement negotiation; benefits here are design estimates.

assumptions: This task applies to representatives selling through retail merchants.
The {SPREADSHEET} commonly joins retailer economics and commercial limits; the {ERP} remains the source of financial records.
Manager approval time is averaged across negotiations; only concessions outside the mandate need that approval.
Terms within the mandate proceed directly to agreement preparation.
Step shares and remaining time are estimates. Store inspection and negotiation retain most of today's effort.
The access range includes financial-data access, GDPR review and applicable employee consultation under national rules. EU AI Act requirements apply where relevant.
unknowns: Whether retailer-level margin and promotional spending are available.
Which concessions require manager or finance approval.
Whether retailer acceptance must use a particular agreement process.
Whether shelf execution can be checked reliably after agreement.
research_questions: Can placement options be calculated from existing financial fields without manual adjustments?
Which agreement terms fit approved templates and which require bespoke drafting?
What evidence distinguishes a worthwhile placement renewal from a poorly performing promotion?
new_work: Maintain commercial limits, calculator assumptions and agreement templates.
Review generated agreements and exceptional concessions.
Check that agreed placements were executed.
Reconcile promotional spending with recorded commitments.

tasks.short: Check stock availability and arrange replenishment when merchandise runs low.

steps.what: Check available stock, reservations and inbound deliveries in the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Combine stock, demand and open purchases in a replenishment {SPREADSHEET}.
Confirm shortages and delivery changes with the warehouse planner by phone.
Calculate replenishment quantities using supplier lead times and reorder settings in the {ERP}.
Review quantities against customer commitments, promotions and unusual demand in the {ERP}.
Approve supplier, quantity and spend in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Release the approved purchase order to the supplier from the {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: First configure native replenishment in the {ERP}; where needed, deterministic links combine {OPS_SYSTEM} stock and {PROCUREMENT} purchase status into an exception view. Validated stock and demand feed reorder rules, representatives review commercial exceptions, and the {PROCUREMENT} releases orders only after purchasing approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales, warehouse and purchasing records update at different times. Manual reconciliation compensates for weak item mappings and unmaintained replenishment settings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reorder features already cover the calculation. AI-assisted coding makes missing status links, validation checks and exception views cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Stock accuracy, unreliable supplier lead times and sudden promotional demand remain operational problems. Rules cannot repair missing physical stock.
tasks.human_edge: The representative recognises customer commitments and unusual demand that have not yet reached the formal records.

ambition.what: Daily shortage prioritisation for customer-critical merchandise.

tasks.altitude: Routine stock checking gives way to short reviews of shortages and unusual demand. The representative gains no purchasing approval rights; the buyer retains spend authority.

reach.task: Give customers reliable availability and delivery commitments.
reach.learn: Available-to-promise stock, reservations, inbound uncertainty and when a delivery date needs confirmation.

evidence.claim: Reorder points, lead times, order multiples and approval limits support deterministic replenishment without a model.
Cross-system stock reconciliation needs stable item identifiers, freshness checks and explicit handling of reservations and inbound deliveries.

assumptions: The representative identifies replenishment needs; a procurement buyer approves supplier commitments.
The {ERP} supports reorder proposals, and the {PROCUREMENT} supports approved-order release.
The {SPREADSHEET} currently bridges stock and purchasing records rather than replacing their source systems.
Step shares and remaining time are estimates. The structured systems and available reorder features support more automation than the human task label suggests.
Warehouse calls become exception-only when stock and delivery status are current.
The access range includes operational and purchasing permissions, GDPR review and any applicable employee consultation under national rules. EU AI Act requirements apply where relevant.
unknowns: Whether the representative reorders owned stock, consignment stock or retailer stock.
Whether native replenishment is licensed and configured.
How accurately reservations, inbound deliveries and physical stock are recorded.
Which supplier orders require approval and which limits apply.
Whether national employee consultation is required for the proposed change.
research_questions: Can native replenishment remove the workbook without custom calculation code?
Which stock and purchasing statuses cause false shortages or duplicate orders?
What freshness and quantity checks should block a replenishment proposal?
new_work: Maintain reorder settings, supplier lead times and item mappings.
Review commercial exceptions and purchasing approvals.
Investigate stale stock feeds, duplicate proposals and failed order releases.
Compare replenishment outcomes with actual shortages and excess stock.

role.altitude: The representative keeps the relationship work: demonstrations, introductions and negotiation. Preparation, record entry and routine replenishment shrink, creating more time for account development and shortage decisions within existing authority.
reach: Order clerks: make sales handoffs complete and availability promises reliable.
Sales managers: compare account coverage and promotional support using consistent evidence.
Procurement buyers: connect customer demand signals to approved replenishment.
skills_to_grow: Product demonstrations shaped around customer use.
Prospect qualification and responsible contact-data use.
Reviewing extracted records against source notes.
Recognising data failures and escalating exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: Become an account development partner who combines trusted customer relationships with current commercial and stock information, offers tailored demonstrations to smaller accounts, and revisits retailer placement choices more often.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products
